title: Joint Limit Chooser
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Safe Control for Robotics
description: Move a torque limit against the torque a task needs and watch a joint hold with margin, hold with little margin, or stall. Then recommend a torque limit for five joint tasks with the rule of thumb: the smallest limit that is at least 1.5 times the need. Used in Chapter 5.

learningObjectives: Recommend the torque limit for each of five joint tasks, choosing the smallest option that is at least 1.5 times the torque the task needs, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Weigh two risks, too little torque and too much, against an explicit margin rule, with feedback on what each option would cause
keyQuestions: What happens when the limit is below the torque the task needs?
Why is the highest limit not the safest choice?
commonMisconceptions: The highest limit is the safest because the joint never fails
The lowest limit is the safest
The limit should equal the torque the task needs
assessmentOpportunities: Five committed recommendations, one attempt each; 4 of 5 for mastery

controls.label: Three torque-limit options for each task
